project: SkyQ San Francisco — prototype v2 (3-day data sprint)
goal: Re-run the SkyQ pipeline on the San Francisco Bay Area, where real ground truth exists, to measure true accuracy instead of estimating it.
why_sf_makes_a_better_prototype: Ground truth: 2,691 Globe at Night records inside the Bay Area box (683 SQM sky-meter readings) vs only 2 in Nineveh — enough to test locally, not just on other regions.
Calibrated satellite data: NASA VNP46A2 / VNP46A4 radiance (nW/cm²/sr) can be downloaded with a free Earthdata account and processed in 1 day, replacing the display images used for Mosul.
Strong dark-sky gradient within 150 km: bright city core (SF, Oakland, San Jose) to certified dark sites (Pinnacles National Park, International Dark Sky Park).
Active local observers (San Francisco Amateur Astronomers, Chabot Space & Science Center, Lick Observatory) for fast field validation.
Different weather problem than Mosul: coastal fog (marine layer) and wildfire smoke instead of desert dust — tests whether the engine generalises.

features.change: All light features in real units (log nW/cm²/sr) from VNP46A2/A4 instead of display-image brightness — no quantile mapping needed
add_for_sf: elevation_m (as a model feature, not only a score bonus)
fraction of lit area within 10 km

labels.priority: SQM readings first; naked-eye only where no SQM exists

model.hybrid: Re-decide the AI + physics mix from validation results instead of fixing it at 50/50

validation.spatial_cv: GroupKFold on 0.25° × 0.25° blocks inside the Bay Area (smaller blocks than Mosul because the area is smaller)
validation.holdout_region: Train on North Bay + East Bay + SF, test on South Bay (San Jose → Mt Hamilton → Coe)
validation.field_test_set: The 3-night SQM campaign readings are NEVER used in training — they are the final exam
validation.rule: Report the measured numbers exactly, even if below target. Do not claim any score before running the test.

decision_engine.weights_note: Starting values only. On day 3, fit the weights to the field-campaign 'good night?' outcomes with a simple logistic regression and report whether they changed.
hard_caps: low cloud (fog) ≥ 70% and site below 400 m → max 25
decision_engine.reachability: ≤ 5 km from a major road AND inside a park/public land that is open at night (check park hours)

three_day_plan.title: Data day
tasks: Create a free NASA Earthdata account; download VNP46A2 (last 30 nights) and VNP46A4 (annual) for tile h05v05.
Convert HDF5 radiance to a 0.02° grid for the Bay Area box (h5py or rasterio); build the median composite.
Filter Globe at Night to US West + Bay Area; apply label rules; keep SQM first.
Fetch elevation and OSM major roads for the Bay Area grid.
Recompute the 11 light features in real units + the new SF features.
three_day_plan.done_when: Every Globe at Night point has features; the Bay Area grid shows SF bright and Pinnacles dark.

three_day_plan.title: Model day
tasks: Train and compare LR / RF / XGBoost with spatial GroupKFold; run the South Bay hold-out.
Recalibrate the physics sky-glow model on the 683 Bay Area SQM readings (leave-one-out error).
Add fog (cloud_cover_low, visibility) and smoke (AOD, pm2_5) to the weather score; switch time zone handling to America/Los_Angeles.
Decide the AI + physics mix from validation, not by hand.
three_day_plan.done_when: Macro-F1, confusion matrix and hold-out results are measured and saved.

three_day_plan.title: Test + app day
tasks: Score the untouched field readings with the model → final Macro-F1 and SQM MAE on brand-new data.
Fit the decision-engine weights to the field 'good night?' outcomes; compare with the starting weights.
Add an English SF version of the app (same 3-question flow) and a region switch Mosul ⇄ San Francisco.
Update the judges' page and README with the measured SF numbers side by side with Mosul.
three_day_plan.output: SF app page, final metrics, README section 'SF vs Mosul'
three_day_plan.done_when: The app answers go / when / where for SF, and every number on the judges' page comes from a real test.

equipment: logging sheet or the app's contribute form
field_campaign.procedure: At each stop: wait 5 min for eyes and meter to settle, take 3 readings pointing at the zenith, record the median + GPS + time + cloud + fog + Moon altitude + Milky Way yes/no.

routes.path: San Francisco → Golden Gate → Mount Tamalpais → Point Reyes
San Jose → Mount Hamilton (Lick) → Henry Coe → Pinnacles

field_campaign.expected_readings: ≈ 30 stops × 3 readings ≈ 90 raw readings (≈ 30 labelled sites)
field_campaign.timing_warning: The Moon was full on 2026-09-26. Moonlight biases SQM readings, so run the campaign around the new moon (conjunction 2026-10-10 15:50 UTC): best nights ≈ 2026-10-08 to 2026-10-12, after astronomical twilight. If it must run earlier, measure only when the Moon is below the horizon and record Moon altitude.
safety: Check park opening hours and permits
Carry warm layers — hilltops get cold and windy
Avoid active wildfire or smoke-advisory areas

must_have: Real Macro-F1 measured on SF data (spatial CV + South Bay hold-out + field test set)
Physics model SQM error in mag/arcsec² on field readings
Working SF app page with the same beginner flow
nice_to_have: Fog-aware best-spot ranking (recommends high sites when the marine layer is low)

risks.risk: Fog or cloud on campaign nights
risks.mitigation: Still log it — foggy nights are useful labels for the weather score; keep a spare night
Schedule around the 2026-10-10 new moon (see timing_warning)

risks.risk: Globe at Night labels are noisy

Report starting vs learned weights; treat learned weights as provisional
